title: Antivirus and EDR vendor alert signals
description: Patterns for malware detections, endpoint isolation and remediation alerts emitted by Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, and compatible antivirus or EDR integrations.

patterns.name: generic threat detected
patterns.explanation: An antivirus or endpoint tool reported a generic threat detection.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because a security product reported a threat that requires immediate triage.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Test samples, simulation modes, and vendor false positives can emit this generic alert.

patterns.name: CrowdStrike detection
patterns.explanation: CrowdStrike reported a detection, prevention, or blocked action.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because an endpoint security control identified or stopped suspicious activity.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Detection test artifacts and benign software blocked by policy can match this pattern.

patterns.name: SentinelOne incident
patterns.explanation: SentinelOne reported a threat, incident, or mitigation event.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because the vendor raised an incident, while the line does not establish impact by itself.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Simulated incidents and vendor classification changes can produce this event.

patterns.name: Defender remediation
patterns.explanation: Microsoft Defender reports that it quarantined or remediated an item.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because a security action occurred and the operator should verify what was changed.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Routine PUA cleanup and approved remediation tests can create the same line.

patterns.name: antivirus signatures updated
patterns.explanation: The antivirus definition set was updated successfully.
patterns.severityRationale: Notice because this is a useful operational event, not an error or threat verdict.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Repeated scheduled updates are expected and may be noisy in routine endpoint logs.
